source.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization
source.authors: Pierre Foret; Ariel Kleiner; H. Mobahi; Behnam Neyshabur

record.tranche_reason: Measures whether m-sharpness tracks generalization gaps, using a different sharpness measure from V7.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that m-sharpness has better correlation with generalization gaps as m decreases. Other SAM-versus-SGD generalization results do not test the listed versions’ specified interventions or comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization connection to motivate SAM, but does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. Its m-sharpness uses norm-bounded perturbations without scaling them to individual weight magnitudes. The other experiments do not test the comparisons specified by V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the m-sharpness subsection: the authors argue that smaller-subset sharpness better predicts generalization gaps and merits further investigation. Their broader conclusion is that SAM improves generalization across many tested vision settings and provides substantial robustness to label noise.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces SAM, minimizing neighborhood-wise loss; it measures m-sharpness rather than the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported association between m-sharpness and generalization varies with m; smaller m is described as yielding better correlation.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.1 reports that m-sharpness predicts generalization gaps better as m decreases on two competition tasks. This is an association involving unscaled perturbations; mutual information alone also does not establish the direction of the association.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness computed over smaller data subsets can predict generalization gaps better than sharpness computed over larger subsets.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM generally improves held-out performance across image-classification and finetuning experiments. Section 4.2 also reports lower Hessian curvature with SAM: the final maximum eigenvalue is approximately 1 versus 24 without SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training with SAM can improve held-out performance and find solutions with lower Hessian curvature than standard training.

record.problems: The m-sharpness correlation results are shown in a figure without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The study reports the association on two competition tasks but the supplied text does not specify the task details.
record.rows_left_out: Other SAM-versus-SGD test error results were not extracted because they do not measure a version's specified intervention or comparison. Figure 3 middle reports test error across rho and m, but not the measured relationship between sharpness and the generalization gap.

untested.parts: Near-perfect random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization and chance performance on held-out random labels. Partial label corruption with clean test labels does not establish this comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, including local connectivity and initialization comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Large versus small optimization batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty. Changing the subset used for SAM perturbations does not establish this comparison.
The effect of adding or removing dropout, including training-set size and augmentation conditions.
The association between magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The rows' cannot_determine states concern their ability to establish V7, not an absence of the reported m-sharpness association. Figure 3's text extraction does not provide exact per-m mutual-information values. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.

The study measures m-sharpness rather than magnitude-aware sharpness; it does not compare the measure with norm- and margin-based measures or test the stated CIFAR-10 and SVHN setting without augmentation.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.
